text.p: Forest products company Boise Cascade Corp. Monday reported a slump in fourth quarter profits, citing an unfavourable paper business, while its office supply affiliate, Boise Cascade Office Products Corp., just nearly matched last year's results.
Boise Cascade said it earned only $2.1 million in the latest quarter compared with a profit of $70.2 million a year earlier. Sales were flat at $1.26 billion.
The company reported a per-share loss of 16 cents after payment of preferred dividends vs. a profit of $1.15 a share a year earlier.
The forest products company, headquartered in Boise, Idaho, said its profits were hurt by a depressed paper market, and it did not anticipate much change in its results early this year.

Meanwhile, Boise Cascade Office Products, based in Itasca, Ill., reported net earnings of $14.4 million or 23 cents a share, vs. year earlier profits of $14.7 million or 24 cents a share. Sales jumped to $556.7 million from $375.0 million.

The distributor of office products, with operations in Australia, Canada, Germany, Britain, and the United States, said it had more than $50 million of same-location sales growth in the fourth quarter and forecast that "1997 should be another good year."
The company also unveiled a joint venture with Germany's Otto Versand -- the world's largest direct marketer of consumer goods.
Otto Versand, which has a $30 million office products catalogue operation, has annual revenues of more than $15 billion.

Boise Cascade Office and Otto Versand will each have a 50 percent equity stake in the venture, the company said. The first marketing project will be in Germany, and the firm said it planned to expand into the other European countries.
In late morning trading, the stock of Boise Cascade fell $1.625 to $36.375, while Boise Cascade Office Products gained 50 cents to $21.50, both on the New York Stock Exchange.
